name: Tokyo
days: 3 (Day 1 arrival/jet lag, Day 2 full day with friend, Day 3 extra day before she flies out)
overview: First stop, together with friend for all 3 days. Friend's only specific ask here is one full day covering the icons plus a Pokemon Center. Everything else is open.

recommendations.title: Shojin ryori
recommendations.summary: Buddhist temple cuisine, fully vegetarian, historically rooted.
recommendations.body: Vegetarian-friendly food is genuinely strong in Tokyo now, but traditional dishes often use dashi (fish stock), so it's worth targeting dishes and restaurants built to be vegetarian rather than assuming. Shojin ryori is Buddhist temple cuisine — fully vegetarian by tradition — and it fits the traditional-sites interest as well as the food one.

recommendations.title: Depachika food halls
recommendations.summary: Department store basement food halls, good for a mixed-diet group.
recommendations.body: Depachika (department store basement food halls) are good for a group with different diets — everyone can pick their own thing rather than sharing one dish.

recommendations.title: Izakaya-style dining
recommendations.summary: Small shareable plates, works well for mixed-diet groups.
recommendations.body: Izakaya-style places work well for a group with different diets — small shareable plates mean everyone can pick their own mix rather than ordering one fixed dish for the table.

recommendations.title: Akihabara
recommendations.summary: Arcades, retro game shops, anime merch, maid cafes.
recommendations.body: Akihabara is the hub for anime, gaming, and pop culture — arcades, retro game shops, anime merchandise, and maid cafes if that's of interest.

recommendations.title: Nakano Broadway
recommendations.summary: Quieter, more collector-focused alternative to Akihabara.
recommendations.body: A quieter, more collector-focused alternative to Akihabara if something less crowded but similar in spirit is wanted.

recommendations.title: Pokemon Center
recommendations.summary: Friend's specific ask — confirm which location before the day it's slotted into.
recommendations.body: Confirm which Pokemon Center location to target — Shibuya, Ikebukuro's Sunshine City, and others all exist. This is friend's one specific request for Tokyo, so worth locking in early.

recommendations.title: teamLab (Planets / Borderless)
recommendations.summary: Immersive digital art, photogenic, fits "iconic in small doses."
recommendations.body: teamLab's immersive digital art exhibits (Planets and/or Borderless) are photogenic and fit the comfort level of iconic spots in small doses.

recommendations.title: Daikanyama / Nakameguro
recommendations.body: Slower, boutique/gallery neighborhoods, less crowded than Shibuya/Harajuku — a design-focused breather if wanted.

recommendations.title: Golden Gai
recommendations.summary: Tiny themed bars in narrow alleys, iconic nightlife.
recommendations.body: Tiny themed bars packed into narrow alleys in Shinjuku — iconic, a good "small dose" of touristy nightlife.

recommendations.title: Shimokitazawa
recommendations.summary: More local, indie bar and vintage shop scene.
recommendations.body: A more local, indie bar and vintage shop scene — less touristy contrast to Golden Gai.

recommendations.title: Asakusa (Senso-ji Temple)
recommendations.summary: Most concentrated traditional atmosphere in central Tokyo.
recommendations.body: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise-dori shopping street give the most concentrated traditional atmosphere in central Tokyo — good, low-key first day, very walkable.

recommendations.title: Meiji Shrine
recommendations.summary: Forested shrine grounds, next to Harajuku.
recommendations.body: Forested shrine grounds right next to Harajuku — also doubles as a real green pocket in the middle of the city (see Nature section).

recommendations.title: Imperial Palace East Gardens
recommendations.summary: Another traditional/historic option if more is wanted.
recommendations.body: Another traditional/historic option if more depth is wanted beyond Asakusa and Meiji Shrine.

recommendations.title: Shinjuku Gyoen
recommendations.summary: Large formal garden park, English/French/Japanese sections.
recommendations.body: A large formal garden park with English, French, and Japanese landscape sections — a step up in scale and quiet from Meiji Shrine if more nature time is wanted.

recommendations.title: Yoyogi Park
recommendations.summary: Open lawns and casual strolling space, adjacent to Meiji Shrine.
recommendations.body: Adjacent to Meiji Shrine, more open lawns and casual strolling space — easy to combine with a Harajuku/Shibuya day.

recommendations.title: Shibuya Crossing
recommendations.body: The famous scramble crossing — good for the shared day with friend, a classic Tokyo icon.

recommendations.title: Harajuku / Takeshita Street
recommendations.summary: Quirky shopping, food stalls, very photogenic.
recommendations.body: Quirky shopping and food stalls, very photogenic, easy walk from Shibuya and Meiji Shrine.

recommendations.title: Omoide Yokocho
recommendations.summary: Tiny alley yakitori stalls in Shinjuku.
recommendations.body: A tiny alley of yakitori stalls in Shinjuku — casual, atmospheric evening food option.

openQuestions: Which specific Pokemon Center location to target
Day 3 direction: food-focused (Tsukiji Outer Market), history-focused, or modern/quirky (Akihabara)
